title: Shadow Traffic MVP – Technical Plan (Routing + Policy + Telemetry + Scoring)
content:
Doc purpose
This is the working technical plan for the Shadow Traffic MVP: mirror a sampled subset of production requests to one or more candidate variants, score the shadow outputs asynchronously, and surface quality deltas without affecting the user response.

Audience: Platform Eng (control plane + routing), Telemetry/Analytics, Applied ML/Evals, Console backend, SRE, Security.

MVP definition (what we will ship)
- Control plane: a “shadow policy” attached to a route and/or rollout object, validated and persisted.
- Data plane: deterministic sampling + mirroring to shadow target(s) with hard timeouts and fail-open behavior.
- Telemetry: emit shadow pair events with strict cardinality controls and safe defaults.
- Scoring: asynchronous queue + workers producing a default metric bundle (v1) using eval-harness adapter (no customer code execution).
- Results: minimal internal dashboard + API query support sufficient for dogfood + limited Dedicated beta.

Non-goals for MVP
- Full offline replay of long-retention historical traffic.
- Customer-provided arbitrary eval code running in Redwood infra.
- Automatic rollback on quality signals (advisory/visibility only for beta, thresholds configured but no automation unless explicitly enabled later).

Key principles / constraints
1) Must not affect user path latency, quotas, or success rate. Shadowing is best-effort and fail-open.
2) Overhead budgets are hard gates (see guardrails). Circuit breakers required.
3) Data minimization and retention by default. Redaction/truncation required for stored artifacts.
4) Deterministic bucketing for consistent comparisons across time windows.

Owners (by workstream)
- Control plane shadow policy schema + validation: Benji Okafor (lead), Ethan Park (review)
- Routing mirror + sampling + bucketing: Ravi Menon (design lead), Vikram Singh (implementation)
- Telemetry event schema + ingestion: Logan Wright (lead), Nadia Rahman (pipelines), Caleb Johnson (ingestion)
- Scoring pipeline + eval-harness adapter: Jonas Weber (lead), Olivia Grant (integration), Selene Huang (metric definitions/alert thresholds)
- Rollouts / experiment object integration: Jada Williams (arch), Chloe Martin (console backend)
- Guardrails / SLOs / oncall readiness: Sean Gallagher (lead), Allison Grant (alerts/dashboards)
- Security / retention / auditability: Marcus Lin (lead)
- Program / cross-team tracking: Talia Benson

Milestones & deliverables (MVP)
Note: dates are illustrative; sequencing and dependency edges are the important part.

Phase 0 – Requirements + architecture alignment (2 weeks)
Deliverables
- Finalize ADR: routing approach + deterministic bucketing + fail-open semantics.
- Finalize ADR: telemetry schema + cardinality limits + safe label set.
- Confirm v1 metric bundle + rubric versioning strategy.
- Confirm retention defaults and redaction approach for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (MVP: Hosted + Dedicated first; Private constraints documented).

Acceptance criteria
- SRE sign-off on fail-open + circuit breaker thresholds.
- Security sign-off on default redaction + retention.

Owners
- ADRs: Ravi Menon + Logan Wright + Marcus Lin; review: Priya Natarajan

Phase 1 – Routing + policy MVP + telemetry events (4–6 weeks)
1A) Control plane: ShadowPolicy schema and storage (ENG-5401)
Deliverables
- ShadowPolicy object stored in control plane config store.
- Validation rules:
  - sampling_rate: 0.0–0.2 (MVP cap; configurable later)
  - max_shadow_targets: 2 (MVP)
  - per-target timeout_ms: 50–250ms range; default 100ms
  - fail_open: always true (cannot be disabled)
  - allowlist for request types: chat.completions + embeddings (MVP); streaming handled in Phase 2 unless low-risk path is ready
  - header/metadata propagation: opt-in allowlist only
- Migration scaffolding for attaching policy to existing Route and Rollout objects.

Notes / open items
- Need a policy composition story: Route.shadow_policy vs Rollout.shadow_experiment shadow policy. Proposal: Rollout-level policy overrides Route policy; route policy is baseline.

1B) Data plane: deterministic sampling + mirroring (ENG-5402, ENG-5403)
Deliverables
- Deterministic request fingerprinting:
  - inputs: tenant_id, route_id, request_type, normalized prompt hash (see privacy notes), optional user_id hash if provided
  - algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant secret salt stored in control plane (prevents cross-tenant correlation)
  - output: 64-bit truncated hash used for bucketing
- Sampling:
  - Bernoulli derived from hash bucket (e.g., hash % 10_000 < sampling_rate*10_000)
  - Stable across retries and time windows
- Mirroring:
  - For sampled requests, send shadow request(s) in parallel with control request, but never await shadow for user response.
  - Strict timeouts and bounded concurrency.
  - Shadow path failures do not count against user request quotas and do not surface to user.

Guardrails (hard requirements)
- Shadow fanout must not exceed 2 targets (MVP).
- Max additional CPU per request on data plane: budgeted and measured in Phase 2 benchmarks.
- Circuit breaker: if shadow target error rate or timeout rate exceeds threshold over rolling window, automatically disable shadowing for that route/tenant for cooling-off period.

1C) Telemetry: event schema + ingestion (ENG-5404, ENG-5410)
Deliverables
- New event types (names TBD but consistent):
  - shadow_request_sent
  - shadow_response_received
  - shadow_pair_scored
- Required dimensions (cardinality-safe):
  - tenant_id (bucketed or internal-only in shared metrics)
  - route_id (hash or short id)
  - control_variant_id (model+version+quant profile)
  - shadow_variant_id
  - experiment_id (optional)
  - region
  - request_type
  - outcome (success/timeout/error)
- Prohibited or restricted dimensions:
  - raw prompt_id, raw user_id, full URL, arbitrary headers
  - any free-form tags from clients
- Storage references:
  - store minimal request/response artifacts via opaque ref ids; actual payload in short-retention store with redaction.

Acceptance criteria
- Cardinality review complete; load tests in staging show no metric blowups at sampling_rate=1% for high-QPS tenant.

Phase 2 – Scoring pipeline + basic dashboards + dogfood (4 weeks)
2A) Async scoring queue + worker (ENG-5405)
Deliverables
- Enqueue scoring job when both control and shadow responses are available (or when shadow arrives and control ref exists).
- Dedupe by (tenant_id, request_fingerprint, shadow_variant_id, rubric_version).
- Retry policy with jitter; DLQ for permanent failures.
- Backpressure: queue depth thresholds trigger circuit breaker to reduce/disable shadow sampling.

2B) Eval-harness adapter + rubric pinning (ENG-5406)
Deliverables
- Adapter transforms shadow pair artifacts into eval-harness job format.
- Rubric version pinned per experiment; default rubric_version=v1.
- Metric bundle v1 (initial proposal; confirm with Applied ML):
  - format_adherence_rate (heuristic + structured output check)
  - refusal_rate (classifier + rules)
  - safety_policy_violation_proxy (heuristic set)
  - instruction_following_score (model-graded rubric; calibrated)
  - verbosity_delta (tokens_out delta as interpretability aid)

Data retention (MVP)
- Raw prompt/response payload retention: 7 days default (Hosted), configurable for Dedicated; Private: follow deployment policy, but MVP only documents constraints.
- Always store hashed fingerprints and aggregate scores beyond raw retention window.

2C) Minimal dashboards + query API (internal)
Deliverables
- Internal-only dashboard for dogfood:
  - volume: sampled requests, shadow success rate
  - scoring lag: p50/p95 time from response_received -> scored
  - quality deltas: control vs shadow by route + variant
- Minimal query endpoints (if needed ahead of Console UI):
  - list experiments (or shadow policies attached)
  - fetch aggregates for a time window
  - fetch sample examples (redacted) with strict RBAC

Acceptance criteria
- Dogfood tenant can run at 1% sampling, 1 shadow target, with scoring lag p95 < 10 minutes.
- No measurable regression on control request p99 latency beyond allowed overhead budget (see below).

Phase 3 – Hardening + beta readiness (4–6 weeks)
Deliverables
- Streaming requests semantics (if in-scope for beta):
  - mirror initial prompt + tool call inputs
  - stop mirroring on client disconnect
  - cap captured output size; partial capture allowed with explicit “partial=true” in telemetry
- Load testing + overhead benchmarks (ENG-5412)
- Feature flag plan and staged rollout (internal -> 1 Dedicated beta -> broader beta)
- Oncall readiness:
  - alerts for scoring lag, queue depth, shadow error rates
  - runbook and kill switches
- Audit logs for config changes (create/update shadow policies and experiments)

Overhead budgets (MVP gates)
- Control request p99 latency delta: <= +1% (absolute budget subject to SRE sign-off; measured in perf-canary suite)
- Router CPU overhead: <= +3% at 1% sampling / 1 shadow target
- Shadow target request timeout default: 100ms; hard cap 250ms
- Shadow path error budget: allowed to be “worse” than control, but must not cascade (circuit breaker)

Dependency mapping (what blocks what)
Legend: A -> B means B cannot complete without A.

Control plane + routing
- ShadowPolicy schema (ENG-5401) -> Router config fetch/apply logic (ENG-5402)
- Bucketing/fingerprint (ENG-5403) -> Deterministic sampling in router (ENG-5402)

Telemetry + scoring
- Telemetry event schema + ingestion (ENG-5404) -> Scoring job creation triggers (ENG-5405)
- Redaction/retention implementation (ENG-5411) -> Example sampling + scoring artifact store (ENG-5405/5406)
- Eval-harness adapter (ENG-5406) -> Metric bundle v1 stable rollup tables

SRE + guardrails
- Circuit breaker/backpressure (ENG-5415) depends on:
  - queue depth metrics (ENG-5405)
  - shadow target timeout/error metrics (ENG-5402/5404)

Console/Rollouts integration
- Experiment object integration (ENG-5413) depends on:
  - shadow policy attach points in control plane (ENG-5401)
  - queryable aggregates (telemetry rollups + scoring outputs)

Risk register (with mitigations)
1) Latency regression on control path due to mirroring overhead
- Risk: router doing extra work per request (hashing, serialization, network fanout) impacts p99.
- Mitigation: strict non-blocking shadow path; bounded concurrency; lightweight fingerprint; sampling cap; perf-canary benchmarks as gate.
- Owner: Ravi Menon / Sean Gallagher

2) Metrics cardinality blowup
- Risk: uncontrolled dimensions (prompt_id, route variants, arbitrary tags) overload observability backend.
- Mitigation: hard dimension allowlist; hash/bucket ids; drop free-form labels; sampling on metrics emission independent of shadow sampling if needed.
- Owner: Logan Wright / Allison Grant

3) Data retention / PII leakage
- Risk: prompt/response payloads can contain PII; storing for scoring/examples creates compliance exposure.
- Mitigation: redact + truncate by default; per-tenant opt-outs; retention defaults short; access restricted + audit logged.
- Owner: Marcus Lin

4) Scoring pipeline cost runaway
- Risk: asynchronous scoring consumes GPU/CPU; high-traffic tenants at 1–5% sampling can exceed cost targets.
- Mitigation: scoring capacity quotas per tenant; adaptive sampling (reduce when queue depth high); metric bundle v1 kept minimal; prioritize heuristic checks over model-graded in high load.
- Owner: Jonas Weber / Karthik Iyer

5) Misleading metrics / statistical noise
- Risk: quality deltas not statistically significant; teams overreact to noise.
- Mitigation: show confidence intervals; minimum sample size warnings; recommend sampling defaults; “insufficient power” status.
- Owner: Sana Farid / Selene Huang

6) Shadow target instability affects downstream systems
- Risk: mirrored traffic increases load on candidate endpoints (especially Dedicated tenants with tight capacity).
- Mitigation: shadow requests count against separate shadow quota; per-route max shadow QPS; default very low sampling; fail-fast timeouts.
- Owner: Cole Summers / Ravi Menon

7) Streaming semantics ambiguous
- Risk: mirroring streaming chats either doubles cost or introduces incorrect partial comparisons.
- Mitigation: defer streaming to Phase 3 unless required for beta; define partial capture explicitly; cap capture size.
- Owner: Vikram Singh

Implementation notes / decisions needed (next 7 days)
- Decide final fingerprint inputs (privacy vs variance reduction). Proposal: HMAC(tenant_salt, route_id + request_type + normalized_prompt_hash + tool_schema_hash). Exclude raw user_id by default.
- Decide whether shadow requests should include original headers by default (proposal: no; allowlist only).
- Decide default scoring rubric version policy (proposal: pinned per experiment; upgrades only on explicit user action).
- Decide Dedicated beta enablement gating: require SRE approval + cost estimate sign-off for sampling>1%.

Testing plan (MVP)
- Unit tests:
  - bucketing determinism across languages/SDKs (router-only source of truth preferred)
  - circuit breaker threshold evaluation
  - schema validation edge cases
- Integration tests:
  - end-to-end: request -> mirrored -> telemetry -> scoring -> aggregate query
  - fail-open: shadow target down, telemetry down, scoring queue down
- Load tests:
  - high-QPS route at 1% sampling; verify control p50/p99 and CPU overhead
  - telemetry ingestion throughput and rollup query latency

Release plan (high level)
- Feature flags:
  - enable_shadow_policy (control plane)
  - enable_shadow_mirroring (router)
  - enable_shadow_telemetry (pipelines)
  - enable_shadow_scoring (workers)
- Stages:
  1) Internal tenant only (dogfood), 0.1% sampling
  2) Internal tenant, 1% sampling, 1 target
  3) 1 Dedicated beta tenant, 0.5–1% sampling, 1 target
  4) Expand beta cohort based on oncall stability and cost

Appendix: Milestone checklist (quick view)
- [ ] ADR routing + fail-open signed off
- [ ] ShadowPolicy schema merged + migrations
- [ ] Router mirroring + bucketing merged
- [ ] Telemetry events merged + cardinality guardrails enforced
- [ ] Scoring queue + workers deployed with backpressure
- [ ] Redaction + retention implemented and verified
- [ ] Dashboards + alerts live; runbook published
- [ ] Perf + overhead benchmarks passing gates

Contact points
- Platform control plane: Benji Okafor / Ethan Park
- Routing: Ravi Menon / Vikram Singh
- Telemetry: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
- Scoring: Jonas Weber / Olivia Grant
- SRE: Sean Gallagher
- Security: Marcus Lin

Notes to self (Benji)
- Keep MVP scoped: 1–2 shadow targets, 0–1% sampling defaults, v1 metric bundle only.
- Be ruthless on cardinality and header propagation. The easiest incident to avoid is the one we never enable by default.
